title: tenant routing header mismatch fix and escalation response
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary: Multiple enterprise customers escalated intermittent 5xx bursts and long tail timeouts across Hosted and Dedicated in the past 48 hours. Symptoms looked like: increased 5xx rate, elevated token latency for streaming calls, and repeated client retries causing request amplification. Root cause analysis identified a recent upstream proxy change in some Dedicated/Private deployments that introduced an extra per-client header (X-Client-Instance) which the serving runtime inadvertently included in cache keys and routing decisions. This header fragmentation caused KV cache miss amplification, longer cold-path kernel selection, and periodic backend overload. The hosted fleet saw cascade amplification because client SDKs retried aggressively without idempotency keys, triggering tenant surge and connection pool exhaustion.

Impact: - Multiple high-value tenants experienced degraded throughput and 5xx spikes during peak usage windows. - Latency-sensitive streaming calls timed out or returned partial responses. - Customer support escalations and an open SRE bridge for 36+ hours.

Root cause details: - A proxy-side rollout added X-Client-Instance to requests for telemetry. - The feeding layer (frontdoor router) forwarded this to the runtime without normalization. - Runtime cache key composition used full header set when computing prefix/KV cache keys. - Result: KV cache sharding dramatically increased cardinality; compaction and eviction were triggered excessively, causing cold-path recomputation. - Coupled with no-per-tenant admission controls and SDKs lacking idempotency/retry tokens, retry storms amplified the problem.

Mitigations and fixes implemented: 1) Emergency mitigation (rolled out within 3 hours): - Deploy ingress normalization to strip X-Client-Instance at the frontdoor for hosted traffic and apply header whitelist for Dedicated control plane. - Add a runtime gate to ignore unknown headers when composing KV cache keys. - Inject temporary per-tenant inflight request cap (soft admission) to dampen bursts. 2) Short-term patch (rolled to canary within 24 hours): - Runtime change: explicit header allowlist for cache/key material and fallback to header-agnostic prefix hashing. - Backport to Dedicated and Private: provide a config flag enable_header_stripping that operators can flip. - SDK guidance: issue client advisory to use Idempotency-Key for non-idempotent calls and update default retry backoff to jittered exponential. 3) Long-term remediation planned: - Formalize header normalization and per-route cache key policy in runtime config with rollout gates. - Add per-tenant fair-queueing and admission controls that consider recent error rates. - Add automated regression tests covering header additions and KV cache cardinality.

Testing and verification: - Canary hosted rollout (us-west-2) with telemetry dashboards to track KV cache hit ratio, eviction rate, mean CPU per worker, and 5xx rate. - Synthetic traffic replay from affected tenants to ensure behavioral parity before/after. - Load tests showing ~60% reduction in cold-path kernel hot swaps and 40% improvements in long-tail p95 token latency under surge patterns.

Rollout plan: - Complete validation in canary by 2026-03-13. - Gradual rollout to remaining hosted regions 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. - Ship backport patch to Dedicated control plane and accompany operator migration guide. - Provide Private bundle and upgrade instructions for air-gapped customers.

Post-incident actions: - Postmortem document to be published in Confluence with timelines and mitigation costs. - Add a continuous test that injects unknown headers into request path to catch regressions. - Update SDKs to include opt-out idempotency header generation for long-running streaming calls. - Customer communications: draft apology + RCA + steps taken and recommended SDK settings.

2026-02-18 18:05 - Priya Desai (Runtime): Found that HeaderSet was passed verbatim into CacheKeyBuilder. Implemented allowlist prototype and unit tests. Patch submitted: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8921.
